textItems.text: Executive coaching for founders, first-time CEOs and the leaders behind them. One hour a fortnight, twelve months, and a measurable change in how your team experiences you.
Six months in, my exec team stopped managing me and started arguing with me. That was the point.

who have outgrown the company they built
in the first year of a bigger seat
one step from the board, and unsure they want it

NOT A FIT: ANYONE LOOKING FOR A CHEERLEADER.

textItems.text: Before we meet I interview six to ten people around you. You get the unedited themes — what they say when you are not in the room.
We pick two or three behaviours that would change the most if they changed. Not ten. Not a personality transplant.
Fortnightly sessions built around real meetings in your diary: the board paper, the hard conversation, the offsite you are dreading.
Short 360 pulses at the start, midpoint and end. The people around you tell us whether it worked. We adjust until they say yes.
Every engagement starts with the same chemistry call and the same question: what would have to be different a year from now?
Land the role before the role lands on you.
A focused engagement for the first quarter in a bigger seat: reading the board, resetting the team you inherited, and deciding what you will be known for.
One hour a fortnight. Twelve months. A different room.
The core engagement. We work on the three or four behaviours that decide how your team experiences you, and we measure them — before, midway and after.
Coach the team that has to carry the strategy.
Team coaching for the layer below the CEO: how you disagree, how you decide, and what happens in the room after the CEO leaves it.
Every engagement is scored by the principal's own team, before and after. These are their numbers, not mine.
AVERAGE SHIFT IN TEAM TRUST SCORE
From the numbers person to the second voice in the room.
Promoted from finance director eight months before an IPO process. We worked on presence with the board and on letting a strong team be strong.
A founder who stopped being the bottleneck.
Forty people, every decision through one inbox. A year later the exec team runs the week and the founder runs the next three years.
Technically brilliant, politically invisible. We built a way of being heard in rooms where the loudest voice usually won.
Leading eleven thousand people through a merger.
Two cultures, one winter. The work was about tempo: what to decide this week, what to refuse to decide, and how to say both out loud.
Names are shortened at clients' request. References are available after a chemistry call.
She is the only person who tells me the truth before the board does.
Six months in, my exec team stopped managing me and started arguing with me. That was the point.
I came for a promotion plan. I left with a different way of running a room.
Helena does not give advice. She asks the question you have been avoiding for a year, then waits.
The 360 was brutal and she made it useful. My team noticed the change before I did.
Before coaching I ran operations for a 900-person business and sat on two boards. I know what Monday morning feels like after a bad Friday board meeting — and I know most of it is fixable.
If the real conversation happens in the corridor, your meeting is theatre. How to move the truth back into the room.
Your first ninety days are not a plan
New CEOs arrive with a deck. The ones who last arrive with questions and a very short list of promises.
The more senior you are, the older your information about yourself. A practical way to shorten the delay.
Tempo is a leadership tool. Some decisions improve with a week; some rot. Telling them apart is the job.

textItems.text: Anything else, ask on the chemistry call — that is what it is for.
What happens on a chemistry call?
Who pays — me or my company?
How is coaching different from mentoring or therapy?
How do you measure whether it worked?
No deck, no pitch. You talk, I listen, and we both find out whether I am the right person for the next year of your working life.
